questions.question_text: Jug A holds a drink with cordial : water $=1:4$. Jug B holds a drink with cordial : water $=1:6$. Which statement must be true?

options.text: Jug B's drink has more water for each part of cordial.
Jug B holds more liquid than jug A.
options.why: Assumes a ratio tells you the total amount, when it only compares the parts.

options.text: Jug A holds more cordial than jug B.
options.why: Reads the first number as an actual amount of cordial rather than a comparison.

options.text: Jug B's drink tastes stronger than jug A's.
options.why: Treats a larger second part as meaning more cordial, when it means more water.

questions.solution_text:
$1:4$ means $4$ parts of water for each part of cordial.
$1:6$ means $6$ parts of water for each part of cordial.
Jug B has more water per part of cordial; neither ratio says how much liquid is in either jug.
